topic.name: Domain and Range of Quadratic Functions

question.text: What is the range of the function $f(x) = -\dfrac{1}{3}(x+2)(x-2)?$
question.explanation:
The given parabola is written in factored form,

\[ y = a(x-x_1)(x-x_2), \]

with $a = -\dfrac{1}{3} < 0.$

Because the leading coefficient is negative, the parabola opens downward. Consequently, there is no minimum output, and the vertex corresponds to the maximum output.

The two roots of the parabola are $x_1=-2$ and $x_2=2,$ and we can find the $x$-coordinate of the vertex by taking the average of the roots: \begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2} = \dfrac{-2+2}{2} = 0 \end{align*}

Then, we substitute $x=0$ back into the function to find the $y$-value of the vertex: \begin{align*} y &= -\dfrac{1}{3}(x+2)(x-2) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{3}(0+2)(0-2) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{3} \cdot 2 \cdot (-2) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{3} \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is $\left( 0,\dfrac{4}{3}\right),$ and the range of the function is $\left(-\infty,\dfrac{4}{3}\right].$

example.title: Finding the Range of a Parabola Given in Factored Form

question.text: What is the range of the function $f(x)=-x^2+6x-8?$
question.explanation:
The given parabola is written in standard form,

\[ y = ax^2+bx+c, \]

with $a=-1< 0,$ $b=6,$ and $c=-8.$

Because the leading coefficient is negative, the parabola opens downward. Consequently, there is no minimum output, and the vertex corresponds to the maximum output.

The $x$-coordinate of the vertex is given by

\[ x= -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{6}{2 \cdot (-1)} = 3. \]

Now, we substitute $x=3$ back into the function to find the $y$-value of the vertex: \begin{align*} y &= -x^2+6x-8 \\[5pt] &= -(3)^2 +6(3)- 8 \\[5pt] &= -9 + 18 - 8 \\[5pt] &= 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is $(3,1),$ and the range of the function is $(-\infty,1].$

example.title: Finding the Range of a Parabola Given in Standard Form

question.text: What is the range of the function $f(x) = -3(x+1)^2-7?$
question.explanation:
The parabola is written in vertex form,

\[ y = a(x-h)^2 + k, \]

where $a$ is the leading coefficient and $(h,k)$ is the vertex.

  • Since $h=-1$ and $k=-7,$ the vertex is $(-1,-7).$

  • Since $a=-3< 0,$ the parabola opens downwards.

Because the parabola opens downwards, there is no minimum output, and the vertex corresponds to the maximum output.

Therefore, the range is $(-\infty,-7].$

example.title: Finding the Range of a Parabola Given in Vertex Form

question.text: Find the range of the function $f(x) = -(x+7)(x+9).$
question.explanation:
The given parabola is written in factored form,

\[ y = a(x-x_1)(x-x_2), \]

with $a = -1 < 0.$

Because the leading coefficient is negative, the parabola opens downward. Consequently, there is no minimum output, and the vertex corresponds to the maximum output.

The two roots of the parabola are $x_1=-9$ and $x_2=-7,$ and we can find the $x$-coordinate of the vertex by taking the average of the roots: \begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2} = \dfrac{-9-7}{2} = -8 \end{align*}

Then, we substitute $x=-8$ back into the function to find the $y$-value of the vertex: \begin{align*} y &= -(x+7)(x+9) \\[5pt] &= -(-8+7)(-8+9) \\[5pt] &= -(-1)\cdot 1 \\[5pt] &= 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the vertex is $\left(-8,1\right),$ and the range of the function is $(-\infty, 1],$ i.e. $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\infty} < f(x) \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\leq} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{1}.$
